Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
301 AM EDT Mon Aug 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 227 AM EDT Monday...

No significant changes were made to the forecast. Shower and
thunderstorm chances are expected this afternoon and evening. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 227 AM EDT Monday...

1. A weak cold front will bring increasing chances of showers
and thunderstorms this afternoon and evening with drier
conditions late Tuesday and Wednesday. 

2.  Widespread showers arrive towards the end of the week, with 
drier conditions expected heading into the weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 227 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: 500 mb flow has gone mostly zonal promoting
weaker variety systems rather than deeply forced events this
week. The next front arrives late this afternoon and will move
through this evening. Upper level support remains anemic with
primary forcing existing in the 850-700mb layer. Timing coupled
with forcing will limit the threat of stronger storms, but CAPE
around 1000j/kg and moderate shear could support a rarer 
stronger cell if it can efficiently tap into low level 
instability or if outflow interacts with the surface front. 
PWATs climbing above 1.5" will favor some heavy shower elements 
and a few cells could produce localized heavy rainfall resulting
in ponding. As noted above, flow will be quite progressive 
leading to a fast exit tonight with drier conditions for 
Tuesday. Northwest flow tonight increases, especially across
Lake Champlain, and may result in some rough lake conditions. 
Dry weather lingers through Wednesday as the Bermuda High 
continues its slow retreat into the Atlantic. Temperatures will 
slowly trend cooler with highs remaining in the mid/upper 70s to
low 80s across northern New York and Vermont. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: A shortwave trough looks to push 
through the region Thursday into Friday, bringing widespread 
shower chances towards the end of the week. Deterministic 
guidance continues to be in good agreement on the general 
pattern evolution, though there is still some uncertainty 
regarding the timing of the system. The current forecast shows 
rain chances ramping up quickly during the early morning hours 
on Thursday with widespread rainfall expected across the upper 
level trough swings through Thursday afternoon. As we get closer
we will have to monitor the potential for a few stronger 
thunderstorms during the afternoon on Thursday, with instability
the biggest question at this time. Behind the trough, a cold 
front is expected to bring below normal temperatures and drier 
weather to the region for Friday into the upcoming weekend. Deep
layer ridging is expected to develop by Saturday which should 
bring plenty of sunshine with highs in the 70s.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 06Z Tuesday...Mainly VFR expected through the period,
with light winds overnight trending southerly 3-7 kts after 12Z
Tuesday. Only exception overnight will be a period of IFR/LIFR 
mist/fog at KMPV, mainly in the 07-13Z time frame. After 18Z 
Tuesday, the approach of a weak disturbance will likely bring 
scattered to widely scattered showers and a few storms, mainly 
to northern areas. Given uncertainty on areal coverage, and 
eventual timing of this activity, have only mentioned at KMSS at
this point.

Outlook...

Tuesday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Likely SHRA, Chance TSRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
